title: Two Killed, Including a Three-Year-Old, as Delhi House Collapses in Jwala Nagar
excerpt: Six tenants were pulled from the Vivek Vihar building in Shahdara and taken to Hedgewar Hospital; officials say the first-floor slab and girder gave way, and the cause is still under investigation.
body:
• Two people, including a three-year-old child, were killed and four others injured when an old house collapsed in Jwala Nagar, Vivek Vihar, in Delhi's Shahdara district on Tuesday morning.
  • Police received the call at about 10:09 a.m.; six tenants were pulled out and taken to Hedgewar Hospital, where two were declared dead.
  • Officials said the first-floor slab and girder of the building, owned by Surendar Singh and occupied by tenants, gave way; no official cause has been established.
  • Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta condoled the deaths and directed departments to ensure the best possible medical care and assistance to the affected families, with no compensation amount announced.

Two people, including a three-year-old child, were killed and four others injured when an old residential building collapsed in Jwala Nagar in east Delhi's Shahdara district on Tuesday, November 17. The collapse, in Gali No. 6 under the Vivek Vihar police station area, was reported to police at about 10:09 a.m., according to ANI via Devdiscourse and Mirror Now.

The rescue

Police, fire department personnel, National Disaster Response Force teams and ambulance services reached the site, and the rescue was carried out with the help of municipal staff and local residents. Six people, all tenants living in the building, were pulled out and taken to Hedgewar Hospital in ambulances, where two were declared dead. Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Shahdara) Geetanjali Khandelwal said the rescued group included a woman and a child, and that two of the injured were slightly critical. Officials quoted in the ANI report said the rescue operation had been completed and no one remained inside the building.

What officials say about the building

Khandelwal said the first-floor slab and girder of the building had collapsed. Municipal Deputy Commissioner Amit Kumar said the building had a ground floor, a first floor and a partially constructed second floor, and was made of stone. The building was owned by Surendar Singh and occupied by tenants. Officials differed on its age: North Municipal Corporation chairman Pankaj Luthra put it at around 40 to 50 years, while Kumar estimated 30 to 40 years. Luthra also said occupants had been asked for years to vacate the building; no notice or document supporting that claim was cited in the reports.

Cause not yet established

No official cause for the collapse has been announced. Police said further investigation and necessary legal proceedings are underway. Bharatiya Janata Party MLA Sanjay Goyal, who visited the site, suggested the building may have fallen due to vibrations from the nearby railway line; that is his claim, not an official finding, and no structural or engineering assessment has been reported.

Government response

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta expressed condolences over the loss of life, said she was closely monitoring the situation, and directed the departments concerned to ensure the best possible medical care and to extend every necessary assistance to the affected families, according to IANS via Hi India. No compensation amount or relief scheme was announced in the reports, and no fundraiser or help channel for the families has been named in the coverage so far.
